suggestions.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
suggestions.description: Randle McMurphy fakes insanity to escape a prison work farm and lands in a psychiatric ward ruled by the iron-willed Nurse Ratched. Jack Nicholson delivers one of cinema's most electric performances as the free spirit who rallies his fellow patients into open rebellion against quiet tyranny. Milos Forman's masterpiece swept all five major Oscars — the last film ever to do so — and stands as a roaring, heartbreaking anthem about freedom, friendship, and the cost of staying yourself. A towering 8.7 classic of 1970s New Hollywood.

suggestions.title: Terminator 2: Judgment Day
suggestions.description: James Cameron reinvents his own monster: the Terminator is back — but this time as protector, reprogrammed to guard young John Connor from the T-1000, a liquid-metal shape-shifter that made 1991 audiences' jaws drop. A landmark of practical effects, relentless set pieces and Linda Hamilton's iconic warrior-woman turn, T2 is the rare sequel that outguns its predecessor at every level — and rewrote what a blockbuster could be. An 8.6-rated adrenaline monument that still defines big-budget filmmaking.

suggestions.title: Inglourious Basterds
suggestions.description: Quentin Tarantino rewrites WWII history with a wink: a squad of Jewish-American soldiers scalps Nazis behind enemy lines while a Jewish cinema owner plots a fiery reckoning in occupied Paris. Christoph Waltz's Oscar-winning Hans Landa — the 'Jew Hunter' — delivers one of the great villain introductions in film history, and the basement-bar scene is pure suspense perfection. Witty, vicious and endlessly quotable, it is an 8.4-rated revenge fantasy built like a powder keg with a film projector for a fuse.
